verdict.rationale: treg has no natural-language interface of its own. It is built to be driven in natural language through the user's coding agent: it ships a first-party Claude connector, an MCP endpoint, a plugin install and an llms.txt that teaches an agent the whole protocol. Its documented workflows are framed as 'give your agent one prompt' and getting results back, and catalog search accepts intent queries ('search by what you want to do'). Missing for 10: a built-in natural-language command interface inside treg itself (NL operation depends on an external agent), and independent hands-on evidence that prompt-driven workflows work as claimed.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Give this to your agent ... $ `set up treg - https://treg.to/llms.txt`
Give your agent one prompt and get back a lead list with a named person, a verified work email and a scored reason to write
[/llms.txt](/llms.txt) is the file to point a coding agent at — it teaches the whole protocol in one fetch.
Search by what you want to _do_, not by vendor: `GET /catalog/search?q=backlinks`.
